items.stem: How is price elasticity of demand calculated?
options: Percentage change in quantity demanded ÷ percentage change in price
Percentage change in price ÷ percentage change in quantity demanded
Change in quantity demanded ÷ change in price
Percentage change in demand ÷ percentage change in income
items.answer: Percentage change in quantity demanded ÷ percentage change in price
items.markingKey: PED = %ΔQd / %ΔP (usually negative).

items.stem: Explain two determinants of the price elasticity of demand for a good.
items.answer: Number and closeness of substitutes (more substitutes → more elastic); proportion of income spent (larger → more elastic); necessity vs luxury; habit/addiction; time period; breadth of definition.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each determinant, 1 mark each explained with direction [4]

items.stem: Explain why the demand for a particular brand of coffee is likely to be more price elastic than the demand for coffee in general.
items.answer: A single brand has many close substitutes (other brands) whereas coffee as a whole has few, so consumers switch brands easily when one brand’s price rises.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: brand has close substitutes; 1 mark: product as a whole has fewer [2]

items.stem: When the price of theatre tickets falls from $25 to $12.50, the quantity demanded rises from 800 to 1,280 units a week. Calculate the price elasticity of demand.

When the price of theatre tickets falls from $40 to $20, the quantity demanded rises from 1,200 to 1,320 units a week. (a) Calculate the price elasticity of demand and state whether demand is elastic or inelastic. (b) Calculate the change in total revenue. (c) Suggest two reasons why demand for theatre tickets might have this elasticity.
items.answer: (a) PED = −0.2: price inelastic. (b) TR $48,000 → $26,400, change −$21,600. (c) Few close substitutes, necessity, habit, small share of income.
items.markingKey: (a) 10/−50 = −0.2 [1]; interpretation [1] (b) 48,000 → 26,400 [2] (c) two consistent reasons [2] [6]

items.stem: When the price of pizzas falls from $12 to $6, the quantity demanded rises from 1,000 to 1,250 units a week. (a) Calculate the price elasticity of demand and state whether demand is elastic or inelastic. (b) Calculate the change in total revenue. (c) Suggest two reasons why demand for pizzas might have this elasticity.
items.answer: (a) PED = −0.5: price inelastic. (b) TR $12,000 → $7,500, change −$4,500. (c) Few close substitutes, necessity, habit, small share of income.
items.markingKey: (a) 25/−50 = −0.5 [1]; interpretation [1] (b) 12,000 → 7500 [2] (c) two consistent reasons [2] [6]

items.stem: Extract: Research for the government of Esteria estimates that the PED for petrol is −0.3, the YED for air travel is +1.8 and the XED between bus travel and the price of petrol is +1.2. The government plans a tax that would raise the price of petrol by 10%. Incomes are forecast to grow by 3% next year. (a) Calculate the expected percentage change in petrol consumption after the tax. (b) Calculate the expected percentage change in demand for bus travel. (c) Calculate the expected change in demand for air travel and explain what the YED value shows.
items.answer: (a) −3% (b) +12% (c) +5.4%; luxury good, demand grows faster than income.
items.markingKey: (a) −0.3 × 10 [1] (b) 1.2 × 10 [1] (c) Credit: +5.4%; luxury good, demand grows faster than income. [2]

items.stem: Extract: Research for the government of Quentara estimates that the PED for petrol is −0.4, the YED for air travel is +1.8 and the XED between bus travel and the price of petrol is +0.8. The government plans a tax that would raise the price of petrol by 15%. Incomes are forecast to grow by 3% next year. (a) Calculate the expected percentage change in demand for bus travel. (b) Explain why the PED for petrol is likely to be inelastic. (c) Calculate the expected change in demand for air travel and explain what the YED value shows.
items.answer: (a) +12% (b) Few close substitutes in the short run, necessity for commuting and business, habit. (c) +5.4%; luxury good, demand grows faster than income.
items.markingKey: (a) 0.8 × 15 [1] (b) Credit: Few close substitutes in the short run, necessity for commuting and business, habit. [2] (c) Credit: +5.4%; luxury good, demand grows faster than income. [2]

items.stem: If PED is −0.4, demand is
items.answer: price inelastic
items.markingKey: |PED| < 1: inelastic.

items.stem: Extract: Research for the government of Calvania estimates that the PED for petrol is −0.4, the YED for air travel is +1.5 and the XED between bus travel and the price of petrol is +1.2. The government plans a tax that would raise the price of petrol by 15%. Incomes are forecast to grow by 3% next year. (a) Calculate the expected percentage change in petrol consumption after the tax. (b) Calculate the expected percentage change in demand for bus travel. (c) Explain why the PED for petrol is likely to be inelastic. (d) Calculate the expected change in demand for air travel and explain what the YED value shows.
items.answer: (a) −6% (b) +18% (c) Few close substitutes in the short run, necessity for commuting and business, habit. (d) +4.5%; luxury good, demand grows faster than income.
items.markingKey: (a) −0.4 × 15 [1] (b) 1.2 × 15 [1] (c) Credit: Few close substitutes in the short run, necessity for commuting and business, habit. [2] (d) Credit: +4.5%; luxury good, demand grows faster than income. [2]

items.stem: If demand is price inelastic, what happens to total revenue when price rises?
items.answer: It rises
items.markingKey: Inelastic: %ΔQ < %ΔP so TR moves with price.

items.stem: Explain why a firm needs to know the PED for its product before changing its price.
items.answer: PED shows whether a price change will raise or lower total revenue: with inelastic demand a price rise raises TR; with elastic demand a price cut raises TR.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: link to TR; 1 mark: elastic vs inelastic case [2]

items.stem: Explain why an indirect tax on a good with inelastic demand may raise revenue but do little to reduce consumption.
items.answer: With inelastic demand the quantity bought falls only a little when the tax raises price, so the tax base stays large (high revenue) and consumption changes little.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: small fall in Q; 1 mark: high revenue/little behaviour change [2]

items.stem: Meridian Group changes the price of its taxi rides from $50 to $55. Weekly sales change from 100 to 95. Calculate the change in total revenue.

Fenwick & Co changes the price of its pizzas from $2 to $1.50. Weekly sales change from 800 to 960. (a) Calculate total revenue before and after the change. (b) Calculate the PED and explain how it accounts for the change in total revenue. (c) Explain why the firm should also consider its costs before deciding on the price.
items.answer: (a) $1,600 → $1,440. (b) PED = −0.8 (price inelastic): price and TR move in the same direction. (c) Profit = TR − TC; a change in output changes total cost, so higher TR does not necessarily mean higher profit.
items.markingKey: (a) both [2] (b) PED [1]; link to TR [1] (c) profit vs revenue [1] [5]

items.stem: Pinnacle plc changes the price of its taxi rides from $12 to $11.40. Weekly sales change from 800 to 824. (a) Calculate total revenue before and after the change. (b) Calculate the PED and explain how it accounts for the change in total revenue. (c) Explain why the firm should also consider its costs before deciding on the price.
items.answer: (a) $9,600 → $9,393.60. (b) PED = −0.6 (price inelastic): price and TR move in the same direction. (c) Profit = TR − TC; a change in output changes total cost, so higher TR does not necessarily mean higher profit.
items.markingKey: (a) both [2] (b) PED [1]; link to TR [1] (c) profit vs revenue [1] [5]

items.stem: Extract: Research for the government of Sundara estimates that the PED for petrol is −0.3, the YED for air travel is +1.5 and the XED between bus travel and the price of petrol is +0.8. The government plans a tax that would raise the price of petrol by 20%. Incomes are forecast to grow by 3% next year. (a) Explain why the PED for petrol is likely to be inelastic. (b) Calculate the expected change in demand for air travel and explain what the YED value shows.
items.answer: (a) Few close substitutes in the short run, necessity for commuting and business, habit. (b) +4.5%; luxury good, demand grows faster than income.
items.markingKey: (a) Credit: Few close substitutes in the short run, necessity for commuting and business, habit. [2] (b) Credit: +4.5%; luxury good, demand grows faster than income. [2]

items.stem: Extract: Research for the government of Istrana estimates that the PED for petrol is −0.3, the YED for air travel is +2.2 and the XED between bus travel and the price of petrol is +0.6. The government plans a tax that would raise the price of petrol by 10%. Incomes are forecast to grow by 3% next year. (a) Calculate the expected percentage change in petrol consumption after the tax. (b) Explain why the PED for petrol is likely to be inelastic. (c) Calculate the expected change in demand for air travel and explain what the YED value shows.
items.answer: (a) −3% (b) Few close substitutes in the short run, necessity for commuting and business, habit. (c) +6.6%; luxury good, demand grows faster than income.
items.markingKey: (a) −0.3 × 10 [1] (b) Credit: Few close substitutes in the short run, necessity for commuting and business, habit. [2] (c) Credit: +6.6%; luxury good, demand grows faster than income. [2]

items.stem: Explain how a firm might make demand for its product less price elastic.
items.answer: Branding and advertising to build loyalty, product differentiation, reducing close substitutes (e.g. by takeovers), loyalty schemes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each method explained [2]

items.stem: A bus company in Dubai raised fares by 20% and its revenue fell. Explain what this suggests about the PED for its services.
items.answer: Revenue fell, so the percentage fall in passengers exceeded 20%: demand is price elastic (|PED| > 1), perhaps because of substitutes such as cars, cycling or rival buses.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: elastic; 1 mark: explanation [2]

items.stem: How is income elasticity of demand calculated?
options: Percentage change in quantity demanded ÷ percentage change in income
Percentage change in quantity demanded ÷ percentage change in price
Percentage change in income ÷ percentage change in quantity demanded
Change in income ÷ change in price
items.answer: Percentage change in quantity demanded ÷ percentage change in income
items.markingKey: YED = %ΔQd / %ΔY.

items.stem: Explain the difference between a normal good and an inferior good, using income elasticity of demand.
items.answer: Normal good: YED positive, demand rises as income rises. Inferior good: YED negative, demand falls as income rises because consumers switch to better-quality alternatives.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Explain why a firm producing a luxury good might be worried about a recession.
items.answer: Luxuries have YED > 1, so a fall in incomes causes a proportionately larger fall in demand and sales.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: YED > 1; 1 mark: large fall in sales [2]

items.stem: Average income in Ostrelia rose from $40,000 to $43,200, and monthly sales of electric scooters changed from 2,000 to 2032 units. Calculate the income elasticity of demand.

Average income in Lunaria rose from $20,000 to $20,800, and monthly sales of restaurant meals changed from 5,000 to 4900 units. (a) Calculate the YED and classify the good. (b) Explain how a discount retailer could use this information if incomes are expected to fall next year.
items.answer: (a) YED = −0.5: inferior good. (b) Sales will rise as incomes fall, so increase stocks/marketing of this good.
items.markingKey: (a) −2%/4% = −0.5 [2]; classification [1] (b) application to falling income [1] [4]

items.stem: Extract: Research for the government of Korvia estimates that the PED for petrol is −0.3, the YED for air travel is +1.8 and the XED between bus travel and the price of petrol is +0.8. The government plans a tax that would raise the price of petrol by 20%. Incomes are forecast to grow by 3% next year. (a) Calculate the expected percentage change in petrol consumption after the tax. (b) Calculate the expected percentage change in demand for bus travel. (c) Explain why the PED for petrol is likely to be inelastic.
items.answer: (a) −6% (b) +16% (c) Few close substitutes in the short run, necessity for commuting and business, habit.
items.markingKey: (a) −0.3 × 20 [1] (b) 0.8 × 20 [1] (c) Credit: Few close substitutes in the short run, necessity for commuting and business, habit. [2]

items.stem: Explain why the same good may be normal for some consumers and inferior for others.
items.answer: At low incomes a good (e.g. bus travel) may be a step up and demand rises with income; at higher incomes people switch to better alternatives (cars), so demand falls.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: income level matters; 1 mark: example [2]

items.stem: Average income in Korvia rose from $40,000 to $43,200, and monthly sales of printed newspapers changed from 1,000 to 1048 units. Calculate the income elasticity of demand.
How is cross elasticity of demand between goods A and B calculated?
options: Percentage change in quantity of A ÷ percentage change in income
Percentage change in quantity demanded of A ÷ percentage change in price of B
Percentage change in price of A ÷ percentage change in quantity of B
Percentage change in quantity of A ÷ percentage change in price of A
items.answer: Percentage change in quantity demanded of A ÷ percentage change in price of B
items.markingKey: XED = %ΔQd(A)/%ΔP(B).

items.stem: Explain how a firm could use cross elasticity of demand when a rival cuts its price.
items.answer: If XED with the rival’s product is high and positive, the firm will lose many sales and may need to respond (cut price or advertise); if low, it can ignore the change.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: high XED → large effect; 1 mark: response [2]

items.stem: Explain why the XED between printers and ink cartridges is negative.
items.answer: They are complements used together; a rise in the price of printers reduces printer sales and so demand for ink falls.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: complements; 1 mark: direction explained [2]

items.stem: When the price of train journeys rises by 5%, the quantity demanded of bus journeys changes from 2,000 to 2020 units a week. Calculate the cross elasticity of demand for bus journeys with respect to the price of train journeys.
items.markingKey: %ΔQ(bus journeys) = +1%; ÷ 5% = 0.2.

items.stem: When the price of streaming subscriptions rises by 20%, the quantity demanded of cinema tickets changes from 4,000 to 4320 units a week. (a) Calculate the XED and identify the relationship between the goods. (b) Explain how a producer of cinema tickets could use this information.
items.answer: (a) XED = 0.4: weak substitutes. (b) Monitor the rival good’s price; if its price rises, expect higher sales (and vice versa); price competitively, advertise to differentiate.
items.markingKey: (a) +8%/20% [1]; sign and strength [1] (b) application [2] [4]

items.stem: Extract: Research for the government of Lunaria estimates that the PED for petrol is −0.3, the YED for air travel is +1.8 and the XED between bus travel and the price of petrol is +0.8. The government plans a tax that would raise the price of petrol by 10%. Incomes are forecast to grow by 3% next year. (a) Explain why the PED for petrol is likely to be inelastic. (b) Calculate the expected change in demand for air travel and explain what the YED value shows.
items.answer: (a) Few close substitutes in the short run, necessity for commuting and business, habit. (b) +5.4%; luxury good, demand grows faster than income.
items.markingKey: (a) Credit: Few close substitutes in the short run, necessity for commuting and business, habit. [2] (b) Credit: +5.4%; luxury good, demand grows faster than income. [2]

items.stem: When the price of bread rises by 10%, the quantity demanded of rice changes from 2,000 to 2040 units a week. Calculate the cross elasticity of demand for rice with respect to the price of bread.
Which factor makes demand for a good more price elastic?
options: The availability of many close substitutes
The good takes a very small share of income
items.answer: The availability of many close substitutes
items.markingKey: Substitutes, luxury, large share of income, longer time period, broad vs narrow definition.

items.stem: Explain what is meant by a PED value of −2.
items.answer: A 1% rise in price causes a 2% fall in quantity demanded; demand is price elastic because the quantity response is proportionately greater than the price change.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: interpretation; 1 mark: elastic [2]

items.stem: The price of cigarettes in Marvona rises by 10% but the quantity bought falls by only 3%. Explain why demand is so unresponsive.
items.answer: Cigarettes are addictive and have few close substitutes, so demand is price inelastic (PED ≈ −0.3).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: PED inelastic value; 1 mark: addiction/few substitutes [2]

items.stem: The PED for T-shirts in Esteria is estimated at −2. Weekly sales are 8,000 units. The price is raised by 8%. Calculate the new weekly sales.
items.answer: 6720 units

items.stem: The PED for haircuts in Kestria is estimated at −0.4. Weekly sales are 8,000 units. The price is cut by 15%. (a) Calculate the percentage change in quantity demanded and the new weekly sales. (b) State and explain whether total revenue will rise or fall.
items.answer: (a) +6%; 8480 units. (b) Demand is inelastic, so TR moves in the same direction as price: falls.

items.stem: Mei, an economics student in Riyadh, is preparing for a class debate on this topic. (a) Explain the factors that determine the price elasticity of demand for a product. (b) Consider whether the availability of substitutes is the most important determinant of PED for bicycles.
items.answer: (a) Substitutes, proportion of income, necessity/luxury, habit, time period, definition of the market; examples; formula. (b) For: Substitutes allow consumers to switch; brands vs product categories. Against: Share of income, addiction, time period also important; depends on the product and consumers; time allows substitutes to emerge. Conclusion: a reasoned judgement on when the claim holds.
items.markingKey: (a) Indicative content: Substitutes, proportion of income, necessity/luxury, habit, time period, definition of the market; examples; formula. Level 3 (6–8): accurate knowledge with a clear, developed analytical chain and, where relevant, an accurate, labelled diagram that is used in the answer; Level 2 (3–5): some correct explanation but undeveloped or partly inaccurate; Level 1 (1–2): limited knowledge, mostly assertion [8] (b) Analysis (AO1/AO2, up to 8): Substitutes allow consumers to switch; brands vs product categories. Evaluation (AO3, up to 4): Share of income, addiction, time period also important; depends on the product and consumers; time allows substitutes to emerge. Top marks need balanced analysis of both sides and a justified conclusion that answers the question set, explaining what the outcome depends on [12]

items.stem: If demand is price elastic, a firm that wants to raise total revenue should
items.answer: cut its price
items.markingKey: Elastic: TR moves opposite to price.

items.stem: A student, Grace, claims: ‘Raising the price always increases a firm’s total revenue.’ Identify what is wrong with this reasoning and give the correct explanation.
items.answer: Only if demand is price inelastic; if demand is elastic, total revenue falls when price rises.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error; 1 mark: correct explanation – Only if demand is price inelastic; if demand is elastic, total revenue falls when price rises. [2]

items.stem: Meridian Group changes the price of its sun hats from $25 to $37.50. Weekly sales change from 100 to 90. Calculate the change in total revenue.
Quarry Bay Ltd changes the price of its taxi rides from $12 to $9. Weekly sales change from 1,000 to 1,300. Calculate the change in total revenue.

Silverline changes the price of its paperback books from $8 to $7.20. Weekly sales change from 500 to 525. (a) Calculate total revenue before and after the change. (b) Calculate the PED and explain how it accounts for the change in total revenue. (c) Explain why the firm should also consider its costs before deciding on the price.
items.answer: (a) $4,000 → $3,780. (b) PED = −0.5 (price inelastic): price and TR move in the same direction. (c) Profit = TR − TC; a change in output changes total cost, so higher TR does not necessarily mean higher profit.
items.markingKey: (a) both [2] (b) PED [1]; link to TR [1] (c) profit vs revenue [1] [5]

items.stem: Extract: Research for the government of Korvia estimates that the PED for petrol is −0.6, the YED for air travel is +1.8 and the XED between bus travel and the price of petrol is +0.8. The government plans a tax that would raise the price of petrol by 15%. Incomes are forecast to grow by 3% next year. (a) Calculate the expected percentage change in petrol consumption after the tax. (b) Discuss whether the petrol tax will achieve both a large rise in tax revenue and a large fall in pollution.
items.answer: (a) −9% (b) Inelastic demand → revenue rises but consumption falls little; conflict between objectives; long-run PED higher (electric cars, buses with XED > 0); estimates uncertain; judgement.
items.markingKey: (a) −0.6 × 15 [1] (b) Credit: Inelastic demand → revenue rises but consumption falls little; conflict between objectives; long-run PED higher (electric cars, buses with XED > 0); estimates uncertain; judgement. [5]

items.stem: A good with a YED of −0.6 is
items.answer: an inferior good
items.markingKey: Negative YED: demand falls as income rises.

items.stem: Borealis plc sells both budget and premium smartphones. Explain why it might shift production towards its premium range as Merania’s economy grows.
items.answer: Premium products likely have higher (positive) YED, so their demand grows faster with incomes, while budget versions may be inferior.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: premium high YED; 1 mark: budget low/negative YED [2]

items.stem: Average income in Westaria rose from $40,000 to $44,000, and monthly sales of printed newspapers changed from 5,000 to 4600 units. Calculate the income elasticity of demand.
A policy institute in Jakarta has published a report on this issue for the government of Istrana. Explain how income elasticity of demand can be used to classify goods.
items.answer: YED formula; negative = inferior; 0–1 = necessity; > 1 = luxury; examples; usefulness for planning.
items.markingKey: Indicative content: YED formula; negative = inferior; 0–1 = necessity; > 1 = luxury; examples; usefulness for planning. items.stem: Explain what the size of XED shows about the relationship between two goods.
items.answer: The larger the absolute value, the stronger the relationship: close substitutes have a large positive XED, close complements a large negative XED; near zero means unrelated.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: magnitude = strength; 1 mark: sign = type [2]

items.stem: Bus fares in Doha rise by 10% and train journeys increase by 4%. Calculate the XED and explain the relationship.
items.answer: XED = +4/10 = +0.4: weak substitutes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: +0.4; 1 mark: substitutes, weak [2]

items.stem: When the price of streaming subscriptions rises by 5%, the quantity demanded of cinema tickets changes from 1,000 to 1020 units a week. Calculate the cross elasticity of demand for cinema tickets with respect to the price of streaming subscriptions.
items.markingKey: %ΔQ(cinema tickets) = +2%; ÷ 5% = 0.4.

items.stem: Freya, an economics student in Santiago, is preparing for a class debate on this topic. Explain how cross elasticity of demand distinguishes substitutes, complements and unrelated goods.
items.answer: XED formula; sign: positive substitutes, negative complements, zero unrelated; magnitude = closeness; examples.
items.markingKey: Indicative content: XED formula; sign: positive substitutes, negative complements, zero unrelated; magnitude = closeness; examples. items.stem: A vertical demand curve has a PED of
items.answer: zero (perfectly inelastic)
items.markingKey: Quantity does not respond to price.

items.stem: An airline cuts fares on the route from Dubai to a holiday island and sales rise sharply. Explain why demand may be price elastic.
items.answer: Holiday flights are a luxury with many substitutes (other airlines, destinations) and take a large share of income, so demand responds strongly.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies elastic; 1 mark: reason [2]

items.stem: In a revision note Ines wrote: ‘Elasticity is the same as the slope of the demand curve.’ Explain what is wrong with this claim.
items.answer: Elasticity measures proportionate (percentage) changes; on a straight-line demand curve the slope is constant but PED varies along it.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error; 1 mark: correct explanation – Elasticity measures proportionate (percentage) changes; on a straight-line demand curve the slope is constant but PED varies along it. [2]

items.stem: At which PED is total revenue unchanged after a small price change?
items.answer: Unitary (−1)

items.stem: The government of Rovania wants to raise more revenue from a tax on airline seats. Explain why PED matters.
items.answer: If demand is inelastic, the tax will reduce sales little and raise more revenue; if elastic, sales fall a lot and revenue may be low.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: inelastic → revenue; 1 mark: elastic → falling base [2]

items.answer: a luxury (income elastic normal) good

items.stem: In a revision note Tomás wrote: ‘A good with a YED of 0.5 is an inferior good because the value is less than one.’ Identify the error in this statement and correct it.
items.answer: A positive YED below 1 shows a normal necessity; a good is inferior only when YED is negative.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error; 1 mark: correct explanation – A positive YED below 1 shows a normal necessity; a good is inferior only when YED is negative. [2]

items.stem: Average income in Kestria rose from $25,000 to $26,000, and monthly sales of smartphones changed from 5,000 to 5040 units. Calculate the income elasticity of demand.

Extract: Research for the government of Quentara estimates that the PED for petrol is −0.4, the YED for air travel is +2.2 and the XED between bus travel and the price of petrol is +0.6. The government plans a tax that would raise the price of petrol by 10%. Incomes are forecast to grow by 3% next year. (a) Calculate the expected percentage change in demand for bus travel. (b) Calculate the expected change in demand for air travel and explain what the YED value shows. (c) Discuss whether the petrol tax will achieve both a large rise in tax revenue and a large fall in pollution.
items.answer: (a) +6% (b) +6.6%; luxury good, demand grows faster than income. (c) Inelastic demand → revenue rises but consumption falls little; conflict between objectives; long-run PED higher (electric cars, buses with XED > 0); estimates uncertain; judgement.

items.stem: Meridian Group makes games consoles and video games. Explain why it might sell consoles at a low price.
items.answer: Consoles and games are complements (negative XED): cheap consoles raise console sales and so raise demand for its profitable games.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: complements; 1 mark: strategy explained [2]

items.stem: Omar wrote in a homework answer: ‘XED measures how the demand for a good responds to a change in its own price.’ Identify the error in this statement and correct it.
items.answer: XED measures the response of demand for one good to a change in the price of another good.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error; 1 mark: correct explanation – XED measures the response of demand for one good to a change in the price of another good. [2]

items.stem: When the price of bread rises by 5%, the quantity demanded of rice changes from 4,000 to 4040 units a week. Calculate the cross elasticity of demand for rice with respect to the price of bread.
